# Proposal Generation Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Proposal Generation Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 22 captured build checkpoints; 6 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 6 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved sales environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded documents, the proposed sales, content, document and Teams connections and the channel; document blocked paths, never bypass them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger; record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for opportunity, content, document and pricing-approval connections with dedicated references. No customer connection is needed for the synthetic workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare bid manager, account executive, sales leader and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer. | Customer or partner |
| Commercial review ownership | Name the pricing approvers and the bid owner who coordinates legal, brand, security and reference review; keep real customer RFPs out of workshop knowledge. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** RFP response work across requirement analysis, content reuse, pricing, references and approvals. Show where fragmented work causes inconsistency and avoidable rework before agreeing success measures.

Fill your baseline record:

| RFP | Measurement period | Requirements tracked | Content sources used | Pricing review steps | Approval steps | Rework cycles | Bid owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree proposal replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Sales business owner | Approve content sources, audience and success measures; keep synthetic prices, margins and win indicators out of customer results. |
| Authorized bid owner and reviewers | Coordinate legal, finance, pricing, security, brand, editorial, reference, sponsor and account-owner review; own customer delivery. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and six skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent in Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before approving any sales connection. |
| Sales content and connection owners | Approve Dynamics 365 Sales, SharePoint, document and pricing-approval connections with dedicated references; own access failures. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check PG-01 through PG-06, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject forbidden side-effect wording and reshoot-required captures. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route commercial decisions to the bid owner. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Proposal replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures have named agreement.
- [ ] The sales owner records how RFP analysis, content, pricing, references and approvals are handled and where rework occurs.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/proposal-generation/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The administrator's data policies cover the proposed sales, content, document and Teams connectors, knowledge sources and intended channel; blocked routes stay blocked.
- [ ] The customer confirms authenticated audience and least-privilege access for opportunity, pricing and content data.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/proposal-generation/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/proposal-generation/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/proposal-generation/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/proposal-generation/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Proposal Generation Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_proposal-generation-operating-rules.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_proposal-generation-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: analyze-rfp
9. Add skill: compile-proposal
10. Add skill: delivery-summary
11. Add skill: executive-summary
12. Add skill: references-positioning
13. Add skill: solution-pricing
14. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
15. Open a fresh Preview conversation
16. Pass PG-01: Bid Manager
17. Pass PG-02: Account Executive
18. Pass PG-03: Sales Leader
19. Pass PG-04: Bid Manager
20. Pass PG-05: Bid Manager
21. Pass PG-06: Sales Leader
22. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: PG-01, PG-02, PG-03, PG-04, PG-05, PG-06. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `ProposalGenerationAgent` and returns `RFP Analysis` and `Evidence boundary`.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, six skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged PG prompt passes once in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges every case on its final response; annotated screenshots are checkpoints, not the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing opportunity, pricing or reference data. Request only the scopes needed for approved sales, content and document systems. Restrict the audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 Sales

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales content and connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 Sales — read:** Add approved read-only opportunity connector actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 Sales:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 Sales:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 Sales:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 6](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Update no CRM record; the win indicator is an illustrative synthetic scenario, not a forecast. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Identify the gap and stop rather than filling it.

### Step 3-2. Integrate SharePoint

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales content and connection owners

1. **Bind SharePoint — read:** Add approved SharePoint content as knowledge with a content owner.

2. **Identity for SharePoint:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope SharePoint:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for SharePoint:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Contact no reference; list reference options with availability checks before use. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Identify the gap and stop rather than filling it.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Microsoft Word and PowerPoint

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales content and connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Word and PowerPoint — write:** Keep outlines as drafts; gate document generation behind an approved workflow (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Word and PowerPoint:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Word and PowerPoint:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Word and PowerPoint:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Create no final document or submission; return a package outline and the required reviews. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, document, approval or message succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Authorized pricing approval workflow

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales content and connection owners

1. **Bind Authorized pricing approval workflow — write:** Hand pricing decisions to the approved workflow; the agent never approves (preview).

2. **Identity for Authorized pricing approval workflow:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Authorized pricing approval workflow:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Authorized pricing approval workflow:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Approve nothing and send nothing; present the discount as a synthetic assumption for authorized pricing review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, document, approval or message succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales content and connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — write:** Keep review items unsent until an approved workflow posts them.

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Contact no reference; list reference options with availability checks before use. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, document, approval or message succeeded.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales content and connection owners

Create dedicated connection references for the approved seams; do not reuse ambiguous existing connections.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved sources preserve grounding and citation boundaries; tools replace skill seams only after identity, authorization, confirmation and success evidence are defined.
- [ ] No CRM write, approval, pricing change, document delivery or customer communication occurs from the agent.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as intended sales users and an unshared identity; a maker's access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic fit scores, prices and margins are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked proposal corpus | All six cases, PG-01 through PG-06, include every required anchor and none of the forbidden wording. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, six skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Commercial authority boundary | Any pricing approval, final document, submission, reference contact, CRM update or customer communication is no-go. |
| Approval gate in every answer | Each response lists unresolved reviewers and states that nothing external changed. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a visible positive anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required captures. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved sales audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed proposal sessions, unsupported claims, connection errors and credit consumption in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

## Deliverables Checklist

### Template provides

- [ ] Agent, synthetic data and component inventory.
- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Adapted mappings, identities, governance and connections.
- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
